steps: Unpack & inspect
Check for shipping damage, confirm the hardware bag and media boxes, remove the pallet screw and set the top plate shims for your finish.

Inspect for shipping damage and report any to your dealer.

Miscellaneous Hardware bag

  • 4 mm hex key (glass frame)
  • Remote control transmitter and wall mount bracket
  • AA batteries, 4
  • Propane fuel conversion kit 156800
  • Vent collar grate inserts
  • Enamel top plate shims, 3

Media and accessory kits ship in separate boxes. Remove the pallet screw (fig. 1).

Top plate shims (fig. 63)

Remove the top plate and the three shims shown. Matte Black: replace the top plate and discard the shims. Linen enamel: install the three separately shipped shims in the same locations, then replace the top plate.

Fit the two side and one front safety barriers over the glass, engaging the mounting tabs over the edges of the cast iron panels.
Location & clearances
Rear 3", sides 7", corner 5", ceiling 16 3/4" from the stove body; alcove max 21 3/4" deep. Approved directly on combustible flooring.

Rear3" (76 mm)
Sides7" (178 mm)
Corner5" (127 mm)
Ceiling16 3/4" (425 mm)
Alcovemax 21 3/4" deep · min 31 1/4" wide · min 62 1/4" ceiling

Plan for heat distribution, vent termination, gas supply routing, traffic areas and a 120V outlet, and leave access for service. Approved directly on combustible floors; a solid surface is recommended.

Mobile home

Secure the stove to the floor with a lag screw or other fastener through the hole in the pedestal base. Install per Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 (U.S.) or CSA Z240.4 (Canada).
Vent system
4/6 direct vent from one approved manufacturer; seal each inner-pipe joint with a 1/8" bead of high-temp sealant or Mil-Pac, never silicone. Own vent only, no common venting.
Vent restriction
Set the exhaust restrictor and intake air shutter (both factory fully open) for the vent zone in fig. 17, then dial in with the burner running. Zone D: CPI only.

Both controls are reached from outside the firebox so the burner can be dialed in while running. Find your zone in the vent termination diagram (fig. 17) and start from its setting.

Exhaust restrictorin the vent adaptor collar; factory fully open
Intake air shutterunder the firebox floor; factory fully open; 1 inch of travel
  • Exhaust: remove the top plate trim rings, loosen the locking screw and turn the pivot plate to the zone's indicator point. After 15 minutes of burner operation, fine-tune in 1/8" increments; don't pass fully closed. Run 10-15 minutes between changes, then tighten the screw and refit the trim rings.
  • Intake: loosen the wingnut, slide the gasketed stem back to half or fully closed, and retighten before lighting.
  • Manual's example: a 20 feet rise with one elbow in a 5 feet horizontal run calls for full restriction.
  • With two or more elbows in a horizontal run, a less restricted setting than the zone diagram may work better.
Zone D terminations: the manual recommends operating only in CPI mode. Where elbows adversely affect IPI, CPI mode should be used.
Glass frame & power cord
Remove the glass frame (four socket-head screws, 4 mm hex key) and discard the labeled lower Skamol retainer. Route the cord through the pedestal without pinching; don't plug in yet.
Gas connection + leak & pressure test
Shut-off and union within 6 feet (T-handle in MA); 3/8" min ID supply. Leak-test with 50/50 soapy water or a gas detector, then check pressures at E and A.

• Gas shut-off valve (gas cock) and union within 6 feet of the stove. Massachusetts: T-handle shut-off (248CMR), installed by a licensed master or journeyman plumber or gas-fitter.
  • Connect at the rear of the base plate or through the floor; supply line 3/8" inside diameter min, or sized to hold pressure at any input setting.
  • Flexible connector where code permits; otherwise the 3/8" iron fitting at the top side of the control valve.
  • Propane-resistant sealing compound on LP units. Leak-test with 50/50 soapy water or a gas detector, never an open flame.
  • Test points on the front of the valve: E = inlet, A = manifold. Test with the regulator control at its highest setting; inlet must not exceed 14.0" WC (1/2 psig).
Fuel conversion / high altitude
Propane: install the included kit 156800 (shipped NG). Natural gas above 2000 ft where the supplier doesn't derate: kit 156822. Never derate propane. Apply the labels.
Firebox panels, media & glass
Skamol panels stay in. Install the chosen media and keep the pilot carry-over ports clear. Refit the glass frame by hand: upper left, lower right, upper right, lower left.

• Skamol panels are factory-installed and must stay in place (they may be painted with high-temperature paint).
  • Optional reflective glass panels 156817: handle with the supplied cotton gloves; rear panel smooth side out, then the side panels behind the retainer wings.
  • River rocks: fragile, support from below; engage the bed on the two center burner pins.
  • StarFire glass: no more than the four pounds (two 2 lb. bags) supplied, spread over the burner plate and rear skirt, crowned toward the center.
  • Log set: center log on the two center pins; left log's narrow end on the rear pin, leaning on the back wall; right log against the upper right corner, slot on the bottom log's pin. Spread the ember stones.
  • Tumbled stones and the Beachfire log set follow their own instructions (kit / Appendix).
  • Keep media off the area in front of the pilot: its carry-over ports must stay clear.
  • Glass frame: wipe the glass, start the screws finger-tight, then tighten upper left, lower right, upper right, lower left with the 4 mm hex key. Never use a power tool.
Initial system check
Plug in, purge the gas line, set Pilot Mode and the Burner switch, confirm the pilot flame, then run every burner, remote and fan function with the homeowner.

Factory-wired and pre-programmed: remote transmitter (3 AAA preinstalled), receiver (4 AA backup preinstalled), switched Fan Control Module. If the build date on the crate label is more than 6 months old, be prepared to replace the receiver and transmitter batteries.

  1. Connect the extension cord to the interior cord and a 120V outlet.
  2. Open the gas supply valve to purge the line; the first lighting takes a few moments.
  3. Set Pilot Mode: CPI (continuous, or Proflame 2 remote) or IPI (intermittent).
  4. Burner rocker switch: ON for manual control and the remote; T-STAT for an optional wall thermostat.
  5. Pilot flame: steady, blue at the hood with yellow toward the edges, engulfing the top 1/8" of the flame sensor, projecting 1" from both ports to the burner plate ports. Tune with the adjustment screw on the front of the valve.
  6. Run every burner, remote and fan function and walk the homeowner through operation.
Flame picture adjustment
Primary air shutter ships at midpoint. Run on high 20-30 minutes, then adjust in 1/8" increments with 10-15 minutes between; closing it too far makes soot.

panels.title: Insufficient gas pressure
items: Little variation in flame between HI and LO regulator settings
Not enough gas for more than one appliance → nuisance outages or gas surges

panels.title: Excessive gas pressure
items: Permanent valve damage → complete appliance shutdown
Pilot flame too large → power generator overheats and shuts down
Sooting from impingement and/or incorrect fuel-to-air mix

panels.title: Flame & soot
items: Very long yellow flames, soot on logs, firebox walls or termination cap → air shutter closed, lack of combustion air
Blue, transparent "anemic" flame → air shutter opened
Weak flame picture, poor combustion or pilot trouble → overly strong draft; add exhaust restriction

panels.title: Pilot & ignition
items: Main burner won't light and the pilot shuts down → no flame rectification at the flame sensor
Pilot can't light at first start-up → air still purging from the gas line
Poor pilot ignition → media covering the carry-over ports in front of the pilot
IPI unreliable with Zone D terminations or elbows → run in CPI mode

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
Your stove lights its own pilot with an electronic igniter. Never try to light the pilot by hand. The Pilot Mode and Burner rocker switches are on the stove's front panel.

  1. Read the safety information. If you smell gas at any point, stop and follow "Safety & gas smell".
  2. Set the thermostat to its lowest setting.
  3. Set the Burner switch to OFF.
  4. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. Then smell for gas, including near the floor.
  5. Set the Pilot Mode switch: CPI keeps the pilot lit for up to seven days; IPI lights the pilot only when there is a call for heat.
  6. Set the Burner switch to ON or T-STAT.
  7. Set the thermostat to the temperature you want. The burner lights.

Day to day, press On/Off on the remote. The pilot lights first, then the burner, and the stove beeps once.

The very first lighting after installation takes a few moments while air clears from the gas line.
If it won't light, turn off the gas to the stove (see "Switches & pilot modes") and call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the Proflame 2 remote
remote.html:
The remote runs the burner, flame height, thermostat, fan and accent lamp. One beep from the stove confirms it got a command. Switch settings for remote use are under "Switches & pilot modes".

  • On/Off turns the burner, fan and lamp on and off. The pilot lights first, then the burner.
  • Up / Down sets flame height (six levels), fan speed and set temperature. Down at the lowest level turns the flame off. Up while the flame is off brings it back at High.
  • Thermostat switches between manual and thermostat control. Keep pressing until "SMART" appears and the stove turns the flame down as the room nears your set temperature.
  • Mode picks what you're adjusting: CPI/IPI, burner, fan or accent lamp.

Room temperature: with the remote off, press Thermostat and Mode together. Child lock: press Mode and Up together; repeat to unlock.

In thermostat mode the stove can turn on suddenly and be very hot even when the burner looks off. Keep the remote out of children's reach.
Note: p. 24 says to re-pair the remote (needed after battery changes) by switching the Burner to OFF, pressing the black (or red) button on the control board, then pressing On within 10 seconds; p. 28 says to put the slider switch in REMOTE, insert a paper clip in the PRG hole on the Receiver cover, then press On.

sounds.title: Sounds, smells and foggy glass
sounds.html:
Creaking and pinging

Cast iron and steel expand and contract as they heat and cool. The creaks and pings you hear are natural thermal movement.

A soft hum

The blower fan hums slightly on its low setting, and the sound grows as the fan speeds up.

Smoke or odor at first

Some smoke and odor is normal during the first several hours of use, while the metal and manufacturing materials cure under heat. It's temporary. Let plenty of fresh air circulate through the room.

Foggy glass

Condensation can form on the glass each time you light the stove. The fog disappears as the glass heats up.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch switches or use a phone in the building, and call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass whenever it needs it, but never while it's hot.

  1. Wipe the surface with a clean, dampened, soft cloth.
  2. Follow with a dry, soft towel.
  3. Take care not to scratch the glass.
Don't use abrasive cleaners or ammonia-based glass cleaner.

Check it while you clean

  • Scratches weaken the glass. If you find any, have the panel replaced.
  • Don't use the stove with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Replacement should be done by a licensed or qualified service person, using only glass from your authorized Jøtul dealer.
  • Don't slam or strike the glass. It can shatter.
  • If a safety barrier screen comes off, put it back before you use the stove.

modes.title: Switches and pilot modes
modes.html:
Pilot Mode switch

CPIpilot stays lit, for up to seven days
IPIpilot lights only when there's a call for heat

After seven days in CPI, the stove switches itself to IPI. Because CPI keeps a flame burning, take care using household products with combustible vapors.

Burner switch

ONmanual burner control; stays here for the remote
T-STATfor an optional wall thermostat
OFFburner off for both remote and manual use

Switch the burner to OFF when you won't use the stove for an extended period.

Note: p. 24 says to set the Pilot Mode switch to CPI for Proflame 2 remote control, after which the remote controls IPI/CPI; the lighting label on p. 41 says to set it to CPI for continuous operation and IPI for thermostatic operation.

To turn off gas to the stove

  1. Set the thermostat to its lowest setting.
  2. Set the Burner switch to OFF.
  3. If service is to be done, turn off all electrical power to the stove.
  4. Close the control access door.

fan.title: Fan and accent lamp
fan.html:
The fan and accent lamp run on house power, so neither works during a power outage.

Fan

  • Press Mode on the remote until the fan icon shows.
  • Use Up / Down to turn the fan on or off or to choose one of six speeds. One beep confirms.
  • A slight hum on low that grows as the fan speeds up is normal.

Accent lamp

  • Press Mode until the AUX icon shows. Up turns the lamp on; Down turns it off.
  • Set the brightness with the dimmer knob on the stove's control panel.
Don't unplug the lamp or fan cords from the Fan Control Module. Use the rocker switch to control power to them.

Changing the bulb

The bulb is a 130V / 50W (PN 222943). Handle it with gloves, because skin oils make it fail early. Replacing it means taking off the glass frame, so shut off the gas and unplug the stove first.

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The stove runs on 120V house current, with a battery pack as backup.

In a power outage

The battery backup still lets the remote run the burner. Flame modulation, thermostat control, the fan and the lamp won't work until power returns. Keep good-quality spare batteries on hand.

Remote3 AAA, 1.5 v
Backup pack4 AA
The manual also prints "6V battery pack (4, AAA)" on p. 23; its spec page (p. 4), battery replacement steps (p. 28) and parts list (p. 37) give 4 AA.

Low-battery signs

  • A battery icon on the remote's screen.
  • No beep from the stove when you press On/Off.
  • A red light on the control board.

Changing the backup batteries

Shut off the gas and unplug the stove first. Switch the Burner to OFF, pull the battery box out of the left side of the control compartment (behind the switch plate), fit four AA batteries, reconnect power and re-pair the remote.

If the batteries are low or dead, the manual says you can still run the burner by sliding the "Receiver switch" to ON. It lights at High.

service.title: Yearly care
service.html:
Have a qualified service technician inspect the stove and its vent system before use and at least once a year.

What the yearly service covers

  • Inspecting and cleaning the whole vent system.
  • Making sure combustion and ventilation air flows freely through the firebox and valve compartment.
  • Checking the pilot assembly for corrosion.
  • Vacuuming the firebox with a soft brush attachment. The logs are fragile.
  • Checking the glass gasket for wear and a good seal, and the glass for scratches.

Between visits

  • Keep the controls and the area under the stove free of dust. Lint from carpeting or bedding can mean more frequent cleaning.
  • Keep the area clear of anything that burns, including gasoline and other flammable liquids.
  • Glass embers can discolor. Wash them in warm, soapy water and dry them thoroughly, or replace them each year.
The ignition system carries live voltage. Always shut off the gas and disconnect power before any maintenance.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Put out any open flame and open windows.
  • Don't light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch or use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone. Follow the gas supplier's instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Around the stove

  • The stove runs very hot. Keep it out of traffic and away from furniture, drapes and clothing.
  • Supervise young children in the room. A child guard or safety gate is recommended if anyone at risk lives with you.
  • The barrier screens over the glass must stay on. If one is damaged, replace it with the manufacturer's barrier for this stove.
  • Burn only natural gas or propane, never wood, paper or other solid fuel.
  • Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician.
  • Don't let anyone use it who doesn't know how it works.
Massachusetts: a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the stove.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser, from the date of purchase. It isn't transferable.

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas & electrical parts (controls, plumbing, valve, blower)1 year

Not covered, in short

  • Wear parts: paint, lamp bulbs, gaskets and glass (unless damaged by thermal stress).
  • Damage from unauthorized modification, use or repair, enamel damage from improper operation or misuse, and damage in transit.
  • Travel time and loss of service.
The warranty is void if installation or service is done by anyone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier, or if the installation doesn't follow the manual and local codes.
Keep your dated sales receipt. Jøtul must get notice of a possible defect within 60 days of when it's found; your authorized Jøtul dealer processes the claim. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

specInput.html:

SIT 885 modulating valve: steps down in six increments between high and low, manually or under the remote's Smart thermostat. Shipped for natural gas; propane kit 156800 is included.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5.0 WC (1.24 kPa) min · 7.0 WC (1.74 kPa) max
Propane12.0 WC (2.99 kPa) min · 14.0 WC (3.48 kPa) max

Measure at test point E on the front of the valve with the valve regulator control at its highest setting. Never let inlet pressure exceed 14.0" WC (1/2 psig): serious valve damage may result. The tools list calls for an external regulator on propane only.

Note: p. 14 says to disconnect the stove and gas control valve from the supply piping during pressure tests above 1/2 psig, and to close the manual shut-off valve for lower test pressures; p. 15 says to close the main manual shut-off valve (gas cock) for tests equal to or above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa).

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure and pilot flame
specManifold.html:
Natural gas1.6 WC (0.398 kPa) min · 3.5 WC (0.87 kPa) max
Propane6.4 WC (1.59 kPa) min · 10.0 WC (2.48 kPa) max

Measure at test point A on the front of the valve, regulator control at its highest setting. Out-of-range symptoms are listed under the pressure faults.

Pilot flame

Steady, not lifting or floating; blue around the pilot hood with traces of yellow toward the outer edges; engulfing the top 1/8" of the flame sensor; projecting 1" from both hood ports to reach the burner plate ports. Tune it with the pilot adjustment screw on the front of the valve.

Hearth: approved for installation directly on combustible floor materials. No additional floor protection is required; a solid surface is recommended.

specVert.title: Vertical venting
specVert.html:
4/6 direct vent from one approved manufacturer only: M&G DuraVent (Direct Vent Pro Series), Selkirk, American Metal Products (Amerivent), Security Chimneys International, Metal-Fab (Sure-Seal Direct Vent), ICC, Bernard Dalsin (Pro Form), Olympia Chimney Supply. Don't mix brands.

Max vent height35 ft. above the appliance
Min vertical termination6 ft. of vent pipe
Elbowsmax two 90° or four 45°
Cap discharge to roof18" (457 mm) min, horizontally
Clearance, all sides1" to combustibles
  • Joints: 1/8" bead of high-temperature sealant or Mil-Pac on the male section of the inner pipe. No silicone.
  • Support offsets every three feet with listed wall straps; listed firestop at every floor penetration.
  • Vertical installations need added exhaust restriction to offset excessive draft (vent restriction step).
  • Own vent system only: never attach to a chimney serving a solid-fuel or gas appliance; common venting is prohibited.
  • Steep roofs, nearby trees or windy sites can cause poor draft or downdraft; more vent height may help.

specHoriz.title: Horizontal and snorkel termination
specHoriz.html:
Min vertical rise off the collarone 24" section of vent pipe
Min horizontal run12" NG · 18" LP
Elbowsmax two 90° or four 45°; cut the horizontal run by 5 feet per additional elbow
Slope1/4" rise per foot toward the cap
Wall cut-out10" × 10" min; 2" clearance at top, 1" on the other sides

Snorkel (natural gas only)

A 90° elbow straight off the rear of the stove is allowed only with a 14" or 36" snorkel cap. 14" snorkel: horizontal run 12" min, no more than a 24" section of pipe. 36" snorkel: 12" min, 5 feet max. Never use a snorkel with propane.

At the cap

  • Don't recess the cap into the wall or siding, and don't insulate the air space around it. Vinyl siding standoff required.
  • Overhead combustible projections: 3" if 2 1/2" or less, 12" if more than 2 1/2". Vinyl siding projections: 18" default.
  • Above grade, veranda, porch, deck or balcony: 12 in. (30 cm). Ventilated soffit within 2 ft of the terminal center line: 18 in. (46 cm). Above a public paved sidewalk or driveway: 7 ft. (2.13 m). Propane tank relief valve / filler: 5 ft. (1.52 m), or 10 ft. (3.05 m) for tanks filled on site from a bulk truck.
  • Window, door, corner, meter, regulator and air-inlet clearances differ for Canadian and U.S. installations; use the fig. 12 table.
  • Don't terminate where frost or ice could build up on adjacent property surfaces.

Allowed rise / run combinations and restrictor zones are in the vent termination diagram (fig. 17).

Note: in the vent terminal clearance table on p. 11, the unventilated soffit (row E) and the Canadian outside and inside corners (rows F and G) are printed as 12 in. with (46 cm), while row D pairs 18 in. with (46 cm).

specElec.title: Electrical and batteries
specElec.html:
Power requirement120 VAC for fan, lamp and burner control module
Fan Control Module120V / 60 Hz
Remote transmitter3 AAA, 1.5 v
Receiver backup4 AA
Power cord10 ft. extension, supplied (157492)
Accent bulb130V / 50W (222943)

The cord in the valve compartment feeds the Fan Control Module, the main power supply for all stove functions. Three-prong grounded plug into a grounded receptacle; never remove the grounding prong. Ground per local code or ANSI/NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. Don't connect to house current until the installation is complete. On battery backup only the burner runs under remote control.

The manual also prints "6V battery pack (4, AAA)" on p. 23; p. 4, 21 and 28, the wiring diagram (p. 29) and the parts list (p. 37) give 4 AA.

specConv.title: Fuel conversion and high altitude
specConv.html:
Shipped for natural gas. Propane kit 156800 is included; the natural gas kit is 156801. A qualified service agency must install it.

Burner orifice#38 NG · #53 LP
Pilot injectorBL .020 NG (226758) · .013 LPG (226759)
High altitude kit, NG156822
NG orifice, 2000-4500 ft.#39 (DMS)

Kit: regulator tower labeled for the fuel, two Torx screws, burner and pilot injectors, Label A (valve compartment), Label B (rating plate), small valve label. Shut off the gas before disconnecting power. Don't over-tighten the burner injector (it can damage the brass elbow and leak). Turn the primary air shutter tube over so the LP or NG indicator faces you. Swap the regulator tower with a Torx T-20. Leak-test, then run the system check.

High altitude

Most gas suppliers derate above 2000 ft. If yours doesn't, install kit 156822 for natural gas (orifice #39 for 2000-4500 ft., 610-1370 m). Do not derate for propane. Fill out the high altitude conversion label and apply it to the rating plate.

conflicts.issue: Receiver backup battery size: 4 AA on p. 4, 21 and 28 (also the 4 AA battery box, p. 37) vs a 6V battery pack of 4 AAA on p. 23. Same note shown in specElec. Settled by the manual: the spec page (p. 4), initial system check (p. 21), battery replacement steps (p. 28), wiring diagram (p. 29: "Battery Pack Four, 1.5v AA") and parts list (p. 37: 157265 battery box, 4 AA) all give 4 AA; guide shows 4 AA with a small note.

Remote initialization differs: p. 24 = Burner switch OFF, black (or red) button on the IFC board, ON within 10 seconds; p. 28 = slider switch to REMOTE, paper clip in the PRG hole on the Receiver cover, then ON. p. 26 (manual by-pass) also names a 'Receiver switch' with an ON position, while p. 21/24 describe control-panel rocker switches (Pilot Mode CPI/IPI; Burner ON/T-STAT/OFF).

Pilot Mode for remote use: p. 24 says set the switch to CPI for Proflame 2 remote control (remote then controls IPI/CPI); the lighting label on p. 41 says CPI = continuous pilot up to seven days, IPI = thermostatic operation.

Isolation during supply-piping pressure tests: p. 14 says disconnect the stove and valve above 1/2 psig and close the manual shut-off below; p. 15 says close the main manual shut-off valve for tests equal to or above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa).
Vent terminal clearance table: rows E, F and G print 12 in. paired with (46 cm), while row D pairs 18 in. with (46 cm).

review.notes: Single combined Installation & Operation manual (139647 Rev 30, 3/25). Catalog BTU (NG 28,000/18,170; LP 24,000/20,750), P.4.1 efficiency (71.14 / 64.13), 4/6 direct vent, mobile-home approval and IPI/CPI all match. Not checkable from the text: heating area, overall dimensions (fig. 2 is a drawing only) and weight. Wiring diagram (p. 29) labels the blower and accent lamp 'Optional', while the rest of the manual treats fan and lamp as part of the system; catalog lists the blower as standard. Catalog feature text says 'black or white glass'; the manual names StarFire Glass Clear (156815) or Black (157342). Scrambled text decoded with the 29-code-point rule: p. 24 MODE key ('controlled: CPI/IPI, Burner, Fan, and Accent Lamp'), 'LCD DISPLAY', 'Blue LCD Screen'; p. 13 'possible, use 45°'. Not decodable and not used: fig. 17 zone labels (p. 13), fig. 41 display labels (p. 24), one line on p. 15. Shown only as diagrams and not transcribed: vent termination diagram with zones and allowed rise/run (fig. 17, p. 13; the text gives no max horizontal run for standard horizontal termination), clearance layouts (figs. 3-5, p. 7), flame pictures (pp. 22, 30), pilot flame pattern (fig. 33). p. 7 vent-pipe clearance list prints 'Alcove - 7" (178 mm)' on the horizontal-run line without saying what it applies to; side and corner clearances are printed as 'from Stove Top'. Pressure-symptom list (p. 15) mentions millivolts and a power generator although this is an IPI stove; transcribed as printed. Burner injector is '#38 mm for NG' on p. 16 but 'Orifice, #38 / NG' on p. 37; guide uses #38. Label A goes on the 'base' (p. 16) vs 'front lip' (p. 17) of the valve compartment. p. 27 lists ceramic glass 156835 side / 156833 front; parts lists give 156834 inner side glass and 156835 outer side glass (pp. 34-35). High-altitude text (p. 18) cites ANSI Z21.88-2005 / CSA 2.33-2005 (cover: 2019 R2024) and gives both 610 - 1371 m and 610-1370 m. Wrong cross-references in the manual: p. 2 break-in 'page 28' (content p. 22); p. 5 info form 'page 38' (p. 40); p. 6 barrier part numbers 'fig. 72, page 34' (157765/157766 are fig. 67, p. 35); p. 9 'page 13' for exhaust restriction (p. 12); p. 15 lighting 'inside back cover' (p. 41); TOC lists 'Masonry Chimney Conversion' p. 9 but no such section exists, and several TOC page numbers are off by one. French-only text not translated: p. 5 glass-door note, p. 16 conversion note, p. 18 altitude sentence, p. 29 wiring caution, p. 31 mobile-home note (English equivalents exist except the p. 18 sentence). The gas-smell block is in English (pp. 1, 41). No LED/error code table in the manual, so codes are empty.
